The curtain above the sink stirred, though the window was closed. A small hand pressed against the glass from outside. It was no bigger than Kit’s, but its fingers were made of shadow.

Kit set down his cup. The drop at its bottom rose, round and bright, until it floated level with his eyes. In its tiny reflection Lina saw the kitchen, the bus, and a child sitting alone in the last row.

The hand slid away from the window.
